TUAN-U-01-01.label: 01 乾 彖辭
TUAN-U-01-01.original: 大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。雲行雨施，品物流形，大明終始，六位時成。時乘六龍以御天，乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。首出庶物，萬國咸寧。
TUAN-U-01-01.essay: The Qian commentary describes the immense creative power of Heaven. All things receive their beginnings from it; clouds move, rain falls, and living forms take shape. The six lines are compared to six dragons moving with the proper times. As the heavenly way changes, each being develops according to its own nature while participating in a larger harmony. The passage ends by connecting this creative order with peace among the many states.

TUAN-U-02-01.label: 02 坤 彖辭
TUAN-U-02-01.original: 至哉坤元，萬物資生，乃順承天。坤厚載物，德合无疆；含弘光大，品物咸亨。牝馬地類，行地无疆，柔順利貞。君子攸行，先迷失道，後順得常。西南得朋，乃與類行，東北喪朋，乃終有慶。安貞之吉，應地无疆。
TUAN-U-02-01.essay: The Kun commentary describes Earth as receptive, spacious, and sustaining. It carries and nourishes all living things by responding to Heaven rather than competing for leadership. The image of a mare conveys endurance and gentle perseverance. A noble person who insists on leading first may lose the way; one who follows the appropriate course finds direction. The references to southwest and northeast, companions and separation, emphasize the importance of position, relationship, and steadfastness.

TUAN-U-03-01.label: 03 屯 彖辭
TUAN-U-03-01.original: 屯，剛柔始交而難生，動乎險中，大亨貞。雷雨之動滿盈，天造草昧，宜建侯而不寧。
TUAN-U-03-01.essay: Zhun concerns the difficulties of a beginning. Firm and yielding forces first meet, producing both the possibility of growth and immediate obstacles. Thunder and rain fill an unsettled world that has not yet found its order. The commentary does not treat the difficulty as a reason to abandon everything. Instead, it urges the establishment of leadership and organization while recognizing that the work of founding a stable order cannot be completed in comfort or haste.

TUAN-U-04-01.label: 04 蒙 彖辭
TUAN-U-04-01.original: 蒙，山下有險，險而止，蒙。蒙亨，以亨行，時中也。匪我求童蒙，童蒙求我，志應也。初筮告，以剛中也。再三瀆，瀆則不告，瀆蒙也。蒙以養正，聖功也。
TUAN-U-04-01.essay: Meng describes ignorance as a condition in which danger is encountered and movement comes to a stop. Yet confusion can be transformed through education when teacher and student respond sincerely to each other. The learner must seek instruction rather than expect it to be imposed. A serious first question deserves an answer, whereas repeated disrespectful questioning undermines the relationship. Cultivating correctness from the beginning is presented as one of education’s most important achievements.

TUAN-U-05-01.label: 05 需 彖辭
TUAN-U-05-01.original: 需，須也，險在前也；剛健而不陷，其義不困窮矣。需，有孚，光亨，貞吉，位乎天位，以正中也。利涉大川，往有功也。
TUAN-U-05-01.essay: Xu means waiting because danger lies ahead. Firm strength does not have to charge into a trap; its strength is shown by remaining steady without becoming trapped. Sincerity, clarity, and a central, appropriate position make waiting purposeful rather than passive. The reference to crossing a great river suggests that action can succeed when the conditions are right. The lesson is to distinguish deliberate preparation from fearful avoidance and reckless advance.

TUAN-U-06-01.label: 06 訟 彖辭
TUAN-U-06-01.original: 訟，上剛下險，險而健，訟。訟，有孚，窒，惕，中吉，剛來而得中也。終凶，訟不可成也。利見大人，尚中正也。不利涉大川，入于淵也。
TUAN-U-06-01.essay: Song concerns disputes arising when danger and forceful assertion come together. Even a person who believes the claim is sincere may encounter obstruction and must remain alert. Stopping the argument before it becomes absolute is preferable to pursuing victory at any cost. The commentary praises an impartial and balanced authority and warns against undertaking a hazardous venture during conflict. Winning an endless quarrel is not the same as resolving it well.

TUAN-U-07-01.label: 07 師 彖辭
TUAN-U-07-01.original: 師，眾也。貞，正也。能以眾正，可以王矣。剛中而應，行險而順，以此毒天下，而民從之，吉又何咎矣。
TUAN-U-07-01.essay: Shi refers to a multitude, particularly an army. The commentary connects legitimate command with correctness: a leader must direct the people toward a defensible purpose. Firmness in the central position is matched by the capacity to secure support. Military action is dangerous and causes suffering, yet its outcome is described as favorable when it is disciplined and undertaken for a proper cause. This is a statement of an ancient political ideal, not a modern endorsement of warfare.

TUAN-U-08-01.label: 08 比 彖辭
TUAN-U-08-01.original: 比，吉也。比，輔也，下順從也。原筮，元永貞，无咎，以剛中也。不寧方來，上下應也。後夫凶，其道窮也。
TUAN-U-08-01.essay: Bi describes people drawing together and offering one another support. Good association requires a trustworthy center and a commitment that can last. People who feel insecure are drawn toward dependable leadership, while those who delay their response may lose the opportunity to join. The commentary explains the favorable judgment through mutual responsiveness between upper and lower positions. Closeness is valuable when it rests on constancy and appropriate relationships.

TUAN-U-09-01.label: 09 小畜 彖辭
TUAN-U-09-01.original: 小畜，柔得位而上下應之，曰小畜。健而巽，剛中而志行，乃亨。密雲不雨，尚往也。自我西郊，施未行也。
TUAN-U-09-01.essay: Xiao Xu presents the accumulation of influence through a relatively small and yielding force. One yielding line occupies an effective position and receives the response of stronger lines. Inner strength works together with outward gentleness so that intentions can gradually be realized. Thick clouds gather without producing rain: the potential is there, but its benefits have not yet appeared. The image emphasizes restraint, accumulation, and the difference between preparation and fruition.

TUAN-U-10-01.label: 10 履 彖辭
TUAN-U-10-01.original: 履，柔履剛也。說而應乎乾，是以履虎尾，不咥人，亨。剛中正，履帝位而不疚，光明也。
TUAN-U-10-01.essay: Lü concerns conduct under demanding conditions. A yielding force moves among stronger ones, and pleasure or harmony responds to the firmness of Heaven. For that reason, walking on a tiger’s tail does not necessarily end in a bite. Success comes through behavior that is appropriately measured rather than merely timid. The commentary also describes firm, centered leadership as bright and free from inward reproach, connecting conduct with moral responsibility.

TUAN-U-11-01.label: 11 泰 彖辭
TUAN-U-11-01.original: 泰，小往大來，吉亨。則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人，君子道長，小人道消也。
TUAN-U-11-01.essay: Tai portrays free communication between Heaven and Earth and between those above and below. When their influences meet, living things flourish and people can share their purposes. The firm and active principle is within, while the yielding and receptive principle is outside. The language of noble and petty people expresses an ancient moral-political order in which worthy conduct gains influence and destructive conduct loses ground. Prosperity depends on connection, not isolation.

TUAN-U-12-01.label: 12 否 彖辭
TUAN-U-12-01.original: 否之匪人，不利君子貞，大往小來。則是天地不交而萬物不通也，上下不交而天下无邦也。內陰而外陽，內柔而外剛，內小人而外君子，小人道長，君子道消也。
TUAN-U-12-01.essay: Pi is the opposite condition: Heaven and Earth cease to exchange their influences, and communication between upper and lower levels fails. The large and constructive principle retreats while the small and obstructive one advances. The commentary pictures a political and social order that cannot function because its parts are disconnected. Worthy people are pushed aside while narrow interests gain strength. The warning concerns the consequences of isolation and the loss of mutual trust.

TUAN-U-13-01.label: 13 同人 彖辭
TUAN-U-13-01.original: 同人，柔得位得中，而應乎乾，曰同人。同人曰，同人于野，亨。利涉大川，乾行也。文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子為能通天下之志。
TUAN-U-13-01.essay: Tong Ren describes fellowship that extends beyond a private faction. A yielding line holds a central position and responds to the strength of Heaven, making common purpose possible. To meet others openly in the fields is to seek cooperation without restricting it to one household or group. Inner clarity and outer strength should be held together through uprightness. The commentary gives the noble person the task of understanding and connecting the aspirations of people throughout the world.

TUAN-U-14-01.label: 14 大有 彖辭
TUAN-U-14-01.original: 大有，柔得尊位，大中而上下應之，曰大有。其德剛健而文明，應乎天而時行，是以元亨。
TUAN-U-14-01.essay: Da You concerns abundance held in a responsible way. A yielding line occupies the honored central position and receives the response of strong lines above and below. Such abundance is not explained by possessions alone. Firm energy, clarity, and action suited to the proper time allow resources and influence to serve a larger order. The commentary associates great success with receptivity at the center and the support of others.

TUAN-U-15-01.label: 15 謙 彖辭
TUAN-U-15-01.original: 謙，亨，天道下濟而光明，地道卑而上行。天道虧盈而益謙，地道變盈而流謙，鬼神害盈而福謙，人道惡盈而好謙。謙尊而光，卑而不可逾，君子之終也。
TUAN-U-15-01.essay: Qian explains why modesty can produce lasting achievement. Heaven lowers what is excessive and raises what is humble; Earth also redistributes what accumulates too high. The passage extends this pattern to spirits and human relations, saying that arrogance attracts opposition while humility wins support. A person in a high position becomes brighter through modesty, while a person in a low position gains dignity. Modesty is presented as a durable principle of conduct.

TUAN-U-16-01.label: 16 豫 彖辭
TUAN-U-16-01.original: 豫，剛應而志行，順以動，豫。豫，順以動，故天地如之，而況建侯行師乎？天地以順動，故日月不過，而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-16-01.essay: Yu joins readiness, harmony, and movement that follows the appropriate time. Firm strength receives a response while action proceeds through receptiveness. The commentary compares this with the orderly movement of sun, moon, and seasons. Government and the use of punishment should also follow an intelligible order, allowing people to accept authority. Establishing political leadership or mobilizing an army is discussed within that ancient framework of timing and collective coordination.

TUAN-U-17-01.label: 17 隨 彖辭
TUAN-U-17-01.original: 隨，剛來而下柔，動而說，隨。大亨貞，无咎，而天下隨時，隨之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-17-01.essay: Sui describes following without surrendering judgment. Firm strength places itself beneath the yielding, and movement is accompanied by a sense of ease. People follow because the relationship is responsive rather than merely coercive. The commentary stresses that the wider world changes with time; successful following therefore requires adjustment to circumstances while keeping to the right course. The meaning of timing is at the center of this hexagram.

TUAN-U-18-01.label: 18 蠱 彖辭
TUAN-U-18-01.original: 蠱，剛上而柔下，巽而止，蠱。蠱，元亨，而天下治也。利涉大川，往有事也。先甲三日，後甲三日，終則有始，天行也。
TUAN-U-18-01.essay: Gu concerns the repair of what has become spoiled through neglect. Strong and yielding forces are positioned in a way that combines penetration with stopping, producing accumulated disorder. Yet the commentary treats the resulting problem as an opportunity for restoring order. Crossing a great river means undertaking necessary work. The days before and after the designated turning point suggest preparation, action, and review. An ending may also be a new beginning.

TUAN-U-19-01.label: 19 臨 彖辭
TUAN-U-19-01.original: 臨，剛浸而長。說而順，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之道也。至于八月有凶，消不久也。
TUAN-U-19-01.essay: Lin describes a growing firm force that approaches and exercises influence. Joyful responsiveness and receptive conduct allow correct action to progress. The commentary also recalls a warning about danger in the eighth month: growth does not continue forever, and what is strong can begin to decline. A favorable period is therefore not a reason for complacency. Its value lies in understanding the cycle of increase and decrease.

TUAN-U-20-01.label: 20 觀 彖辭
TUAN-U-20-01.original: 大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。觀，盥而不荐，有孚顒若，下觀而化也。觀天之神道，而四時不忒，聖人以神道設教，而天下服矣。
TUAN-U-20-01.essay: Guan is about observation and the influence of an example. Those in prominent positions should view the world with receptiveness, humility, and fairness. The ritual image of washing before the offering portrays a solemn attitude that invites respect even before the ceremony is complete. The commentary also considers the regular movement of the seasons. From such patterns, it explains how moral instruction can emerge through visible conduct rather than force alone.

TUAN-U-21-01.label: 21 噬嗑 彖辭
TUAN-U-21-01.original: 頤中有物，曰噬嗑，噬嗑而亨。剛柔分，動而明，雷電合而章。柔得中而上行，雖不當位，利用獄也。
TUAN-U-21-01.essay: Shi He describes a blockage that must be bitten through before communication can resume. Firm and yielding forces are distinct, and vigorous movement is joined with clear perception, like thunder together with lightning. The commentary applies this image to deciding judicial cases, where determination must be matched by understanding. It is an ancient account of punishment and legal order, not a license for arbitrary severity.

TUAN-U-22-01.label: 22 賁 彖辭
TUAN-U-22-01.original: 賁，亨；柔來而文剛，故亨。分剛上而文柔，故小利有攸往。剛柔交錯，天文也；文明以止，人文也。觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。
TUAN-U-22-01.essay: Bi concerns ornament, pattern, and culture. Yielding and firm forces decorate or temper one another, producing a limited but genuine capacity for progress. The patterned interplay of forces is called the order of Heaven; cultivated clarity and restraint become the order of human affairs. By observing natural patterns, people recognize changes in season and time. By attending to human culture, they develop customs and forms of education that shape social life.

TUAN-U-23-01.label: 23 剝 彖辭
TUAN-U-23-01.original: 剝，剝也，柔變剛也。不利有攸往，小人長也。順而止之，觀象也。君子尚消息盈虛，天行也。
TUAN-U-23-01.essay: Bo portrays a process of stripping away. Yielding forces steadily replace the firm, making forward movement unwise. The commentary advises recognizing this tendency and knowing when to stop. The noble person observes increase and decline, fullness and emptiness, as recurring features of the natural order. When a structure is losing its support, forcing progress may only deepen its instability.

TUAN-U-24-01.label: 24 復 彖辭
TUAN-U-24-01.original: 復亨；剛反，動而以順行，是以出入无疾，朋來无咎。反復其道，七日來復，天行也。利有攸往，剛長也。復其見天地之心乎？
TUAN-U-24-01.essay: Fu describes the return of firm, life-giving energy. Movement begins again and proceeds in a receptive way, so coming and going need not cause harm. The image of return after seven days expresses a recurring rhythm rather than a fixed promise of immediate success. The commentary associates the moment with growth and asks whether the renewal of life reveals something of the heart of Heaven and Earth.

TUAN-U-25-01.label: 25 无妄 彖辭
TUAN-U-25-01.original: 无妄，剛自外來，而為主於內。動而健，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之命也。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。无妄之往，何之矣？天命不佑，行矣哉？
TUAN-U-25-01.essay: Wu Wang means acting without falsehood or reckless intention. Firm strength enters and becomes the central influence, joining movement with vigor. Appropriate action is described as aligned with the order of Heaven. Yet an act that departs from correctness invites trouble, even if it appears energetic. The commentary questions the value of proceeding when conduct no longer agrees with the right course.

TUAN-U-26-01.label: 26 大畜 彖辭
TUAN-U-26-01.original: 大畜，剛健篤實輝光，日新其德，剛上而尚賢。能止健，大正也。不家食吉，養賢也。利涉大川，應乎天也。
TUAN-U-26-01.essay: Da Xu concerns the storing and disciplining of great strength. Firmness, substantiality, and brightness are joined with daily renewal of character. The ability to restrain force is itself a major form of correctness. Honoring capable people and supporting their service beyond the private household bring the strength to public use. Crossing a great river represents undertaking significant work with resources and timing properly aligned.

TUAN-U-27-01.label: 27 頤 彖辭
TUAN-U-27-01.original: 頤貞吉，養正則吉也。觀頤，觀其所養也；自求口實，觀其自養也。天地養萬物，聖人養賢，以及萬民；頤之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-27-01.essay: Yi examines nourishment in both its material and ethical senses. To nourish rightly means observing what is supported and how a person provides for themselves. Heaven and Earth sustain living things; a wise ruler supports the capable and cares for the wider population. The commentary treats nourishment as a serious responsibility: what people feed, cultivate, and maintain reveals their values.

TUAN-U-28-01.label: 28 大過 彖辭
TUAN-U-28-01.original: 大過，大者過也。棟橈，本末弱也。剛過而中，巽而說行，利有攸往，乃亨。大過之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-U-28-01.essay: Da Guo describes a situation whose burden has exceeded its ordinary support. A roof beam bends because its ends are weak even though the middle is strong. The commentary does not say that all action must stop. Firmness can still be balanced by a yielding manner and a readiness to meet others. Extraordinary pressure calls for extraordinary discernment, especially about whether the supporting structure can bear the weight.

TUAN-U-29-01.label: 29 坎 彖辭
TUAN-U-29-01.original: 習坎，重險也。水流而不盈，行險而不失其信。維心亨，乃以剛中也。行有尚，往有功也。天險不可升也，地險山川丘陵也，王公設險以守其國，坎之時用大矣哉！
TUAN-U-29-01.essay: Kan concerns repeated danger. Flowing water enters difficult places without losing its nature, offering an image of faithfulness under pressure. Inner strength remains central, and successful action requires an honest understanding of risk. The commentary also considers natural barriers in the sky and landscape, along with defensive works established by rulers. Danger must be understood, navigated, and sometimes used for protection.

TUAN-U-30-01.label: 30 離 彖辭
TUAN-U-30-01.original: 離，麗也；日月麗乎天，百谷草木麗乎土，重明以麗乎正，乃化成天下。柔麗乎中正，故亨；是以畜牝牛吉也。
TUAN-U-30-01.essay: Li means attachment or dependence. The sun and moon are attached to Heaven, while grasses and grains depend on Earth. Light achieves its purpose when it is connected to what is right. A yielding line in a central and correct position allows clarity to operate without harshness. The image of raising a gentle cow connects successful cultivation with patient, receptive steadiness.

TUAN-L-31-01.label: 31 咸 彖辭
TUAN-L-31-01.original: 咸，感也。柔上而剛下，二氣感應以相與，止而說，男下女，是以亨利貞，取女吉也。天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平；觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣！
TUAN-L-31-01.essay: Xian means mutual influence or response. Yielding and firm forces meet, and the two energies affect one another. Stillness combines with joy, and the man’s deferential approach to the woman belongs to the passage’s ancient marriage symbolism. The commentary broadens the theme: Heaven and Earth respond and produce life; wise people respond to human feeling and support peace. Observing relationships reveals how beings influence one another.

TUAN-L-32-01.label: 32 恆 彖辭
TUAN-L-32-01.original: 恆，久也。剛上而柔下，雷風相與，巽而動，剛柔皆應，恆。恆亨无咎，利貞；久于其道也，天地之道，恆久而不已也。利有攸往，終則有始也。日月得天，而能久照，四時變化，而能久成，聖人久于其道，而天下化成；觀其所恆，而天地萬物之情可見矣！
TUAN-L-32-01.essay: Heng means continuity. Thunder and wind work together, while firm and yielding lines find their counterparts. Constancy is not mere immobility; it is commitment to a right course through continuing change. The sun and moon shine through regular movement, and the seasons complete their cycles by changing. The commentary asks what a person remains faithful to over time, since duration has value only when it serves an appropriate principle.

TUAN-L-33-01.label: 33 遯 彖辭
TUAN-L-33-01.original: 遯亨，遯而亨也。剛當位而應，與時行也。小利貞，浸而長也。遯之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-33-01.essay: Dun concerns withdrawal at the proper time. Retreat is not automatically defeat: it may be the very means of preserving a worthwhile course. Firm strength still occupies an appropriate position, but a growing yielding influence alters the circumstances. Small matters can remain stable while broader confrontation becomes unwise. The commentary highlights the importance of recognizing when to step back.

TUAN-L-34-01.label: 34 大壯 彖辭
TUAN-L-34-01.original: 大壯，大者壯也。剛以動，故壯。大壯利貞；大者正也。正大而天地之情可見矣！
TUAN-L-34-01.essay: Da Zhuang describes strength at its height. Firm energy is capable of decisive movement, but true greatness requires righteousness. The commentary rejects the assumption that power alone makes an action appropriate. Its final statement connects what is great and upright with the deeper character of Heaven and Earth.

TUAN-L-35-01.label: 35 晉 彖辭
TUAN-L-35-01.original: 晉，進也。明出地上，順而麗乎大明，柔進而上行。是以康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接也。
TUAN-L-35-01.essay: Jin means advancement. Brightness rises above the Earth, and receptive conduct aligns itself with what is illuminating. A yielding line rises into an influential position. The narrative of a lord receiving horses and frequent audiences with the king illustrates recognition and promotion in an ancient political setting. Advancement is meaningful when it follows clarity and responsive conduct.

TUAN-L-36-01.label: 36 明夷 彖辭
TUAN-L-36-01.original: 明入地中，明夷。內文明而外柔順，以蒙大難，文王以之。利艱貞，晦其明也，內難而能正其志，箕子以之。
TUAN-L-36-01.essay: Ming Yi depicts light going beneath the Earth and becoming obscured. Inner clarity may need to be protected by outward modesty during great hardship. The commentary invokes King Wen and Jizi as figures who endured danger without abandoning their inner commitments. Difficulty is not interpreted as a reason to surrender correctness; sometimes wisdom requires keeping one’s light out of view.

TUAN-L-37-01.label: 37 家人 彖辭
TUAN-L-37-01.original: 家人，女正位乎內，男正位乎外，男女正，天地之大義也。家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。父父，子子，兄兄，弟弟，夫夫，婦婦，而家道正；正家而天下定矣。
TUAN-L-37-01.essay: Jia Ren discusses order within a household through the roles recognized by ancient society. Its statements about men and women reflect historical family arrangements rather than a universal modern rule. Parents are expected to guide the family, and each relationship carries responsibilities. The commentary connects orderly family conduct with the stability of the larger political community.

TUAN-L-38-01.label: 38 睽 彖辭
TUAN-L-38-01.original: 睽，火動而上，澤動而下；二女同居，其志不同行；說而麗乎明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛；是以小事吉。天地睽，而其事同也；男女睽，而其志通也；萬物睽，而其事類也；睽之時用大矣哉！
TUAN-L-38-01.essay: Kui concerns difference and separation. Fire moves upward while water in the marsh moves downward, suggesting directions that do not naturally coincide. Even people who share a home may have different purposes. The commentary nevertheless points out that Heaven and Earth remain jointly productive despite differences. The lesson is not that all distinctions disappear, but that a limited form of cooperation may still be possible.

TUAN-L-39-01.label: 39 蹇 彖辭
TUAN-L-39-01.original: 蹇，難也，險在前也。見險而能止，知矣哉！蹇利西南，往得中也；不利東北，其道窮也。利見大人，往有功也。當位貞吉，以正邦也。蹇之時用大矣哉！
TUAN-L-39-01.essay: Jian means obstruction. Danger lies ahead, and the ability to stop upon recognizing it is called wisdom. The directions southwest and northeast symbolize different degrees of practical difficulty. Seeking the help of a capable person and preserving the right position are both praised. The passage places discernment and support above stubborn persistence.

TUAN-L-40-01.label: 40 解 彖辭
TUAN-L-40-01.original: 解，險以動，動而免乎險，解。解利西南，往得眾也。其來復吉，乃得中也。有攸往夙吉，往有功也。天地解，而雷雨作，雷雨作，而百果草木皆甲坼，解之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-40-01.essay: Jie describes release from difficulty through timely movement. After a danger has been resolved, returning to an ordinary position can be fortunate; when necessary tasks remain, acting early can produce results. The commentary compares release to thunder and rain breaking a period of confinement, allowing plants to emerge and grow. Removing an obstruction restores possibilities that had been held back.

TUAN-L-41-01.label: 41 損 彖辭
TUAN-L-41-01.original: 損，損下益上，其道上行。損而有孚，元吉，无咎，可貞，利有攸往。曷之用？二簋可用享；二簋應有時。損剛益柔有時，損益盈虛，與時偕行。
TUAN-L-41-01.essay: Sun describes reduction, especially the transfer of resources or influence from below to above. Sincere reduction can be appropriate, but it must occur at the right time and in the right measure. The commentary uses a modest ritual offering to show that simplicity may express genuine reverence. Firmness and yielding, gain and loss, fullness and emptiness are all adjusted in response to the time.

TUAN-L-42-01.label: 42 益 彖辭
TUAN-L-42-01.original: 益，損上益下，民說无疆，自上下下，其道大光。利有攸往，中正有慶。利涉大川，木道乃行。益動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。
TUAN-L-42-01.essay: Yi means increase. The passage describes benefit flowing from above to those below, creating broad satisfaction among the people. Those in authority become more effective when they support others rather than merely accumulate resources. Correct and central action brings favorable results. Just as a boat enables a river crossing, well-directed benefit creates new practical possibilities. Increase should follow changing circumstances.

TUAN-L-43-01.label: 43 夬 彖辭
TUAN-L-43-01.original: 夬，決也，剛決柔也。健而說，決而和，揚于王庭，柔乘五剛也。孚號有厲，其危乃光也。告自邑，不利即戎，所尚乃窮也。利有攸往，剛長乃終也。
TUAN-L-43-01.essay: Guai describes a decisive break. A strong majority confronts a remaining obstacle, but judgment should be public and truthful rather than driven by aggression. The court and the local community are settings for making the danger known. Resorting immediately to arms is discouraged. The commentary favors a firm but measured resolution of conflict when the time has become ripe.

TUAN-L-44-01.label: 44 姤 彖辭
TUAN-L-44-01.original: 姤，遇也，柔遇剛也。勿用取女，不可與長也。天地相遇，品物咸章也。剛遇中正，天下大行也。姤之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-44-01.essay: Gou means encountering. Yielding and firm forces unexpectedly meet, creating both generative possibility and a warning about allowing one influence to grow unchecked. The marriage language belongs to the traditional symbolism of the text. The commentary also observes that Heaven and Earth meet and living things take form. What matters is the character and consequence of an encounter.

TUAN-L-45-01.label: 45 萃 彖辭
TUAN-L-45-01.original: 萃，聚也；順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。王假有廟，致孝享也。利見大人亨，聚以正也。用大牲吉，利有攸往，順天命也。觀其所聚，而天地萬物之情可見矣。
TUAN-L-45-01.essay: Cui means gathering. People come together when receptive conduct, mutual pleasure, and a reliable center work in concert. The ruler’s visit to an ancestral temple is an image of shared ritual and common belonging. Yet gathering must serve a proper purpose and recognize legitimate leadership. The commentary invites attention not only to the number of people assembled but also to what draws them together.

TUAN-L-46-01.label: 46 升 彖辭
TUAN-L-46-01.original: 柔以時升，巽而順，剛中而應，是以大亨。用見大人，勿恤；有慶也。南征吉，志行也。
TUAN-L-46-01.essay: Sheng means rising or gradual ascent. Yielding strength advances according to its time, supported by modest conduct and a strong central response. Visiting a capable leader is favorable; movement toward the south symbolizes a purposeful journey. The commentary understands growth as something achieved by steady alignment, not by forceful self-promotion.

TUAN-L-47-01.label: 47 困 彖辭
TUAN-L-47-01.original: 困，剛掩也。險以說，困而不失其所，亨；其唯君子乎？貞大人吉，以剛中也。有言不信，尚口乃窮也。
TUAN-L-47-01.essay: Kun describes confinement, especially the obscuring of firm strength. A person can still preserve an inner sense of rightness while facing severe constraints. The commentary praises the noble person who remains true to position and principle. A central, firm character matters more than an abundance of explanations, for words alone cannot restore trust when circumstances have become difficult.

TUAN-L-48-01.label: 48 井 彖辭
TUAN-L-48-01.original: 巽乎水而上水，井；井養而不窮也。改邑不改井，乃以剛中也。汔至亦未繘井，未有功也。羸其瓶，是以凶也。
TUAN-L-48-01.essay: Jing uses the image of a well. A town may change, but the well continues to nourish those who come and go. The essential resource remains useful only if it can be drawn and shared. An unfinished draw or a broken vessel defeats the effort just before success. The commentary distinguishes enduring public value from the practical work required to make that value accessible.

TUAN-L-49-01.label: 49 革 彖辭
TUAN-L-49-01.original: 革，水火相息，二女同居，其志不相得，曰革。巳日乃孚；革而信也。文明以說，大亨以正，革而當，其悔乃亡。天地革而四時成，湯武革命，順乎天而應乎人，革之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-49-01.essay: Ge describes transformation when opposed forces can no longer remain as they are. Water and fire conflict, suggesting a need for change. Reform gains trust only when its time has arrived. The commentary links rightful change with the turning of the seasons and with ancient political revolutions. Change without legitimacy is unstable; change undertaken at the proper time can resolve regret.

TUAN-L-50-01.label: 50 鼎 彖辭
TUAN-L-50-01.original: 鼎，象也。以木巽火，亨飪也。聖人亨以享上帝，而大亨以養聖賢。巽而耳目聰明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛，是以元亨。
TUAN-L-50-01.essay: Ding uses the ritual cooking vessel as an image of nourishment and ordered transformation. Wood feeds fire, and the vessel prepares offerings for the divine and food for worthy people. The commentary links receptive intelligence with an effective central position. Great success comes not from the vessel itself but from the proper use of resources in service of ritual and community.

TUAN-L-51-01.label: 51 震 彖辭
TUAN-L-51-01.original: 震，亨。震來虩虩，恐致福也。笑言啞啞，后有則也。震驚百里，驚遠而懼邇也。出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。
TUAN-L-51-01.essay: Zhen means shaking or thunder. Sudden fear can become the beginning of care and good fortune if it leads to disciplined conduct. After the shock, one may recover enough composure to speak and laugh. The thunder that startles distant and nearby people becomes an image of leadership able to maintain its duties even under disturbance.

TUAN-L-52-01.label: 52 艮 彖辭
TUAN-L-52-01.original: 艮，止也。時止則止，時行則行，動靜不失其時，其道光明。艮其止，止其所也。上下敵應，不相與也。是以不獲其身，行其庭不見其人，无咎也。
TUAN-L-52-01.essay: Gen means stopping. The appropriate action is not always motion: there are times to halt and times to proceed. True clarity depends on acting and resting at the right moment. The commentary describes stopping where one should stop and letting go of self-centered attachment. The absence of mutual entanglement between the lines makes freedom from blame possible.

TUAN-L-53-01.label: 53 漸 彖辭
TUAN-L-53-01.original: 漸之進也，女歸吉也。進得位，往有功也。進以正，可以正邦也。其位剛，得中也。止而巽，動不窮也。
TUAN-L-53-01.essay: Jian, meaning gradual progress, likens orderly advancement to a marriage conducted according to accepted rites. Reaching the proper position makes constructive achievement possible. Inner stillness and outward gentleness allow progress without exhaustion. The text connects personal development and public order through the idea that a stable result requires a suitable process.

TUAN-L-54-01.label: 54 歸妹 彖辭
TUAN-L-54-01.original: 歸妹，天地之大義也。天地不交，而萬物不興，歸妹人之終始也。說以動，所歸妹也。征凶，位不當也。无攸利，柔乘剛也。
TUAN-L-54-01.essay: Gui Mei treats marriage and the continuation of generations as a major relationship between Heaven, Earth, and humanity. Yet the marriage described here is marked by problematic positions and an imbalance between yielding and firm forces. Acting simply because one is pleased does not guarantee a good outcome. The commentary reflects ancient marriage conventions while examining the consequences of a relationship entered under unsuitable conditions.

TUAN-L-55-01.label: 55 豐 彖辭
TUAN-L-55-01.original: 豐，大也。明以動，故豐。王假之，尚大也。勿憂宜日中，宜照天下也。日中則昃，月盈則食，天地盈虛，與時消息，而況于人乎？況于鬼神乎？
TUAN-L-55-01.essay: Feng means abundance or greatness. Brightness joined with vigorous movement produces a flourishing condition. A ruler at the height of prosperity is compared to the midday sun, whose light reaches far. Yet the very same image also warns that the sun must decline after noon and the full moon must wane. Prosperity and change are inseparable.

TUAN-L-56-01.label: 56 旅 彖辭
TUAN-L-56-01.original: 旅，小亨，柔得中乎外，而順乎剛，止而麗乎明，是以小亨，旅貞吉也。旅之時義大矣哉！
TUAN-L-56-01.essay: Lü concerns the traveler, who lacks a fixed home and has only limited resources. A yielding line occupies the central position outside, cooperating with firm strength. Stillness and attachment to clarity permit modest progress. A traveler can act successfully by remaining correct and cautious, but the situation is not the same as secure residence.

TUAN-L-57-01.label: 57 巽 彖辭
TUAN-L-57-01.original: 重巽以申命，剛巽乎中正而志行。柔皆順乎剛，是以小亨，利有攸往，利見大人。
TUAN-L-57-01.essay: Xun describes repeated penetration and the careful transmission of instructions. Firm strength remains responsive to central correctness, while yielding lines cooperate with it. The result is limited but workable progress. Seeing a capable person and undertaking measured action are favorable because influence grows through persistence and clarity rather than sudden force.

TUAN-L-58-01.label: 58 兌 彖辭
TUAN-L-58-01.original: 兌，說也。剛中而柔外，說以利貞，是以順乎天，而應乎人。說以先民，民忘其勞；說以犯難，民忘其死；說之大，民勸矣哉！
TUAN-L-58-01.essay: Dui means joy and openness. Firmness is held within while yielding appears outwardly, so pleasant conduct need not abandon principle. When leaders foster confidence and shared purpose, people may willingly undertake work and face hardship. The commentary presents joy as a powerful social bond when grounded in correctness and genuine human response.

TUAN-L-59-01.label: 59 渙 彖辭
TUAN-L-59-01.original: 渙，亨。剛來而不窮，柔得位乎外而上同。王假有廟，王乃在中也。利涉大川，乘木有功也。
TUAN-L-59-01.essay: Huan concerns dispersal and the removal of blockage. Firm strength does not become trapped, and yielding influence finds an appropriate position. The ruler’s temple represents a common center that can reassemble people after division. Crossing a great river by boat illustrates movement made possible by suitable means. Dispersal can therefore clear a path toward renewed connection.

TUAN-L-60-01.label: 60 節 彖辭
TUAN-L-60-01.original: 節，亨，剛柔分，而剛得中。苦節不可貞，其道窮也。說以行險，當位以節，中正以通。天地節而四時成，節以制度，不傷財，不害民。
TUAN-L-60-01.essay: Jie describes measured limits. Firm and yielding positions are differentiated, while central firmness prevents arbitrary excess. Severe restriction that causes needless suffering cannot last. Proper limits, by contrast, help institutions function and protect resources. Just as the seasons arise through orderly divisions, a good system sets bounds without exhausting wealth or harming the people.

TUAN-L-61-01.label: 61 中孚 彖辭
TUAN-L-61-01.original: 中孚，柔在內而剛得中。說而巽，孚，乃化邦也。豚魚吉，信及豚魚也。利涉大川，乘木舟虛也。中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。
TUAN-L-61-01.essay: Zhong Fu concerns inner sincerity. Yielding forces lie within, while firmness occupies central positions; openness and humility make trust effective. The image of even small creatures being reached by sincerity expresses how far integrity may extend. A hollow wooden boat can cross a river, linking inner openness with practical action. Sincerity becomes valuable when joined with correctness.

TUAN-L-62-01.label: 62 小過 彖辭
TUAN-L-62-01.original: 小過，小者過而亨也。過以利貞，與時行也。柔得中，是以小事吉也。剛失位而不中，是以不可大事也。有飛鳥之象焉，有飛鳥遺之音，不宜上宜下，大吉；上逆而下順也。
TUAN-L-62-01.essay: Xiao Guo concerns a slight excess that may be acceptable in small matters but dangerous in major ones. Yielding lines occupy central positions while firm lines are poorly placed. The bird in flight symbolizes the risk of rising too high. The commentary recommends lowering one’s aim and adapting to circumstance rather than taking on an undertaking beyond one’s capacity.

TUAN-L-63-01.label: 63 既濟 彖辭
TUAN-L-63-01.original: 既濟，亨，小者亨也。利貞，剛柔正而位當也。初吉，柔得中也。終止則亂，其道窮也。
TUAN-L-63-01.essay: Ji Ji means completion. The lines stand in comparatively appropriate positions, allowing limited success and initial good fortune. Yet completion creates its own danger: if vigilance stops, order may deteriorate into confusion. The commentary cautions that a favorable beginning is not a guarantee of an enduring result.

TUAN-L-64-01.label: 64 未濟 彖辭
TUAN-L-64-01.original: 未濟，亨；柔得中也。小狐汔濟，未出中也。濡其尾，无攸利；不續終也。雖不當位，剛柔應也。
TUAN-L-64-01.essay: Wei Ji means not yet completed. Even without an ideal arrangement of the lines, firm and yielding forces respond to one another. The small fox almost crosses the stream but wets its tail before reaching safety. The image warns against losing care at the final stage. Because completion has not yet been achieved, appropriate effort and mutual response remain necessary.

XIANG-U-01-01.label: 01 乾 大象
XIANG-U-01-01.original: 天行健，君子以自強不息。
XIANG-U-01-01.essay: Heaven moves with unflagging strength. A responsible person takes this image as a reason to cultivate character and keep improving without giving up.

XIANG-U-01-02.label: 01 乾 小象 1
XIANG-U-01-02.essay: The hidden dragon should not yet act because the yang line remains at the bottom. Its strength exists, but the appropriate occasion to display it has not arrived.

XIANG-U-01-03.label: 01 乾 小象 2
XIANG-U-01-03.essay: The dragon appearing in the field signifies virtue spreading outward. Worthy conduct is beginning to benefit people beyond the individual.

XIANG-U-01-04.label: 01 乾 小象 3
XIANG-U-01-04.essay: Working diligently throughout the day means repeatedly returning to the proper course. Constant effort must be guided by principles rather than mere activity.

XIANG-U-01-05.label: 01 乾 小象 4
XIANG-U-01-05.essay: The dragon poised to leap from the depths can advance without blame. It is beginning to act at the moment when advancement is appropriate.

XIANG-U-01-06.label: 01 乾 小象 5
XIANG-U-01-06.essay: The flying dragon in Heaven signifies the emergence of a capable and virtuous leader. The time has come for such a person to accomplish important work.

XIANG-U-01-07.label: 01 乾 小象 6
XIANG-U-01-07.essay: The dragon soaring too high brings regret because fullness cannot last indefinitely. Excessive ascent, however impressive, eventually meets its limit.

XIANG-U-01-08.label: 01 乾 小象 7
XIANG-U-01-08.essay: The use of all nine lines teaches that heavenly virtue does not depend on any one dragon claiming supremacy. Strength is best exercised without a contest for first place.

XIANG-U-02-01.label: 02 坤 大象
XIANG-U-02-01.original: 地勢坤，君子以厚德載物。
XIANG-U-02-01.essay: Earth receives and supports everything with its depth and breadth. The exemplary person learns from it to develop generous character and carry the needs of others.

XIANG-U-02-02.label: 02 坤 小象 1
XIANG-U-02-02.original: 履霜堅冰，陰始凝也。馴致其道，至堅冰也。
XIANG-U-02-02.essay: The first frost shows that yin has begun to condense. As this small change advances gradually, hard ice will follow; beginnings therefore deserve attention.

XIANG-U-02-03.label: 02 坤 小象 2
XIANG-U-02-03.original: 六二之動，直以方也。不習无不利，地道光也。
XIANG-U-02-03.essay: The movement of the second yin line is straight and square. Its natural conduct is beneficial without rehearsal because the way of Earth is clear and open.

XIANG-U-02-04.label: 02 坤 小象 3
XIANG-U-02-04.original: 含章可貞，以時發也。或從王事，知光大也。
XIANG-U-02-04.essay: Keeping excellence within and remaining steadfast means releasing one’s gifts at the right time. Serving the ruler without claiming achievement shows a broad understanding of duty.

XIANG-U-02-05.label: 02 坤 小象 4
XIANG-U-02-05.essay: Tying up the mouth of the sack avoids blame because careful restraint prevents harm. There are moments when silence offers better protection than display.

XIANG-U-02-06.label: 02 坤 小象 5
XIANG-U-02-06.essay: The yellow lower garment is greatly auspicious because its refinement is held within. Modest appearance can express centered, balanced character.

XIANG-U-02-07.label: 02 坤 小象 6
XIANG-U-02-07.essay: Dragons fighting in the open field show that this course has reached an impasse. When opposing forces become extreme, conflict is difficult to avoid.

XIANG-U-02-08.label: 02 坤 小象 7
XIANG-U-02-08.essay: Perseverance in the use of six is favorable because it enables a great completion. Receptive strength fulfils its work through steadfast continuity.

XIANG-U-03-01.label: 03 屯 大象
XIANG-U-03-01.essay: Clouds and thunder mark the difficulty of beginnings. The exemplary person responds by untangling confusion, organizing affairs, and laying the foundations of good government.

XIANG-U-03-02.label: 03 屯 小象 1
XIANG-U-03-02.original: 雖磐桓，志行正也。以貴下賤，大得民也。
XIANG-U-03-02.essay: Although progress is hesitant, the intention remains directed toward what is right. A person of higher standing gains the people’s support by humbly approaching those below.

XIANG-U-03-03.label: 03 屯 小象 2
XIANG-U-03-03.original: 六二之難，乘剛也。十年乃字，反常也。
XIANG-U-03-03.essay: The difficulty of the second line comes from a yielding line riding a firm one. The long delay before marriage reflects an eventual return to an ordinary, fitting course.

XIANG-U-03-04.label: 03 屯 小象 3
XIANG-U-03-04.original: 即鹿无虞，以從禽也。君子舍之，往吝窮也。
XIANG-U-03-04.essay: Pursuing deer without a guide means chasing prey blindly. The wise person abandons the pursuit because pressing onward would end in frustration.

XIANG-U-03-05.label: 03 屯 小象 4
XIANG-U-03-05.essay: Going forward to seek the marriage shows discernment. The act becomes favorable because the purpose and occasion are finally clear.

XIANG-U-03-06.label: 03 屯 小象 5
XIANG-U-03-06.essay: The rich nourishment cannot yet be shared widely, so its beneficial effects remain limited. Resources alone do not guarantee that help reaches others.

XIANG-U-03-07.label: 03 屯 小象 6
XIANG-U-03-07.essay: Tears of blood flow in the final line: how could such distress continue? Endless paralysis and grief cannot provide a sustainable way forward.

XIANG-U-04-01.label: 04 蒙 大象
XIANG-U-04-01.original: 山下出泉，蒙；君子以果行育德。
XIANG-U-04-01.essay: A spring flows from beneath the mountain. Seeing this image of youthful uncertainty, the exemplary person acts decisively while patiently nurturing moral character.

XIANG-U-04-02.label: 04 蒙 小象 1
XIANG-U-04-02.essay: Corrective discipline is useful when it establishes a clear rule. Education should release people from ignorance rather than impose punishment for its own sake.

XIANG-U-04-03.label: 04 蒙 小象 2
XIANG-U-04-03.essay: The son’s ability to manage the household arises when firmness and gentleness connect. Successful guidance requires these complementary qualities.

XIANG-U-04-04.label: 04 蒙 小象 3
XIANG-U-04-04.essay: The warning against taking the woman concerns conduct that does not proceed in the proper way. Attraction without integrity leads to an unsuitable union.

XIANG-U-04-05.label: 04 蒙 小象 4
XIANG-U-04-05.essay: The distress of ignorance results from being isolated from what is real. Refusing instruction and remaining distant from trustworthy knowledge brings regret.

XIANG-U-04-06.label: 04 蒙 小象 5
XIANG-U-04-06.essay: The fortunate childlike learner is receptive and modest. Willingness to learn is more valuable than pretending to know everything.

XIANG-U-04-07.label: 04 蒙 小象 6
XIANG-U-04-07.essay: Defending against bandits succeeds because higher and lower positions cooperate. Proper correction protects people instead of turning force into aggression.

XIANG-U-05-01.label: 05 需 大象
XIANG-U-05-01.original: 雲上於天，需；君子以飲食宴樂。
XIANG-U-05-01.essay: Clouds gather above Heaven, but the rain has not yet arrived. The exemplary person waits without agitation, enjoying ordinary food, fellowship, and rest.

XIANG-U-05-02.label: 05 需 小象 1
XIANG-U-05-02.original: 需于郊，不犯難行也。利用恆，无咎，未失常也。
XIANG-U-05-02.essay: Waiting in the outskirts avoids entering danger prematurely. Maintaining a steady way of life prevents mistakes and preserves one’s proper course.

XIANG-U-05-03.label: 05 需 小象 2
XIANG-U-05-03.original: 需于沙，衍在中也。雖小有言，以終吉也。
XIANG-U-05-03.essay: Waiting on the sand allows room for movement without losing balance. Minor criticism need not spoil an ultimately favorable outcome.

XIANG-U-05-04.label: 05 需 小象 3
XIANG-U-05-04.original: 需于泥，災在外也。自我致寇，敬慎不敗也。
XIANG-U-05-04.essay: Waiting in the mud places one close to trouble; the threat is still outside. If one has attracted attackers, alert and respectful caution may prevent defeat.

XIANG-U-05-05.label: 05 需 小象 4
XIANG-U-05-05.essay: Waiting amid bloodshed calls for a willingness to heed circumstances. Listening and yielding appropriately offers a path away from immediate peril.

XIANG-U-05-06.label: 05 需 小象 5
XIANG-U-05-06.essay: Food and drink during the wait are favorable because the person occupies a balanced and proper position. Composure is not the same as neglect.

XIANG-U-05-07.label: 05 需 小象 6
XIANG-U-05-07.original: 不速之客來，敬之終吉。雖不當位，未大失也。
XIANG-U-05-07.essay: Unexpected visitors are treated respectfully, and the ending is fortunate. Though the position is not ideal, the essential requirements have not been seriously lost.

XIANG-U-06-01.label: 06 訟 大象
XIANG-U-06-01.original: 天與水違行，訟；君子以作事謀始。
XIANG-U-06-01.essay: Heaven and water move in opposing directions, portraying contention. Before beginning an undertaking, the exemplary person carefully considers its origins and terms.

XIANG-U-06-02.label: 06 訟 小象 1
XIANG-U-06-02.original: 不永所事，訟不可長也。雖小有言，其辯明也。
XIANG-U-06-02.essay: Not prolonging the dispute acknowledges that contention should not endure. Minor objections may arise, but the issues can eventually be clarified.

XIANG-U-06-03.label: 06 訟 小象 2
XIANG-U-06-03.original: 不克訟，歸逋竄也。自下訟上，患至掇也。
XIANG-U-06-03.essay: An unsuccessful litigant withdraws and takes refuge. A subordinate who persists in suing a superior readily brings trouble upon himself in this historical setting.

XIANG-U-06-04.label: 06 訟 小象 3
XIANG-U-06-04.essay: Living on inherited virtue and following those above can end favorably. One should undertake service without insistently demanding personal credit.

XIANG-U-06-05.label: 06 訟 小象 4
XIANG-U-06-05.essay: Changing course after a failed dispute means returning to one’s proper obligations. Peaceful constancy keeps a person from greater loss.

XIANG-U-06-06.label: 06 訟 小象 5
XIANG-U-06-06.essay: Judging a lawsuit with great good fortune rests on fairness and balance. Justice requires a decision rooted in what is centered and right.

XIANG-U-06-07.label: 06 訟 小象 6
XIANG-U-06-07.essay: An official robe won through litigation is not worthy of honor. A contentious victory does not by itself establish moral respectability.

XIANG-U-07-01.label: 07 師 大象
XIANG-U-07-01.original: 地中有水，師；君子以容民畜衆。
XIANG-U-07-01.essay: Water lies within Earth, like a gathered force held in reserve. The exemplary person receives the people generously and fosters their shared strength.

XIANG-U-07-02.label: 07 師 小象 1
XIANG-U-07-02.essay: An army must depart under discipline. When military order breaks down, the expedition risks misfortune, whatever its intentions.

XIANG-U-07-03.label: 07 師 小象 2
XIANG-U-07-03.original: 在師中吉，承天寵也。王三錫命，懷萬邦也。
XIANG-U-07-03.essay: Good fortune for the commander comes from receiving the ruler’s trust. Repeated appointments also impose responsibility for protecting the many states.

XIANG-U-07-04.label: 07 師 小象 3
XIANG-U-07-04.essay: An army returning with corpses has accomplished nothing worthy of praise. Poor command is measured by human loss as well as failure of objectives.

XIANG-U-07-05.label: 07 師 小象 4
XIANG-U-07-05.essay: Withdrawing and encamping to one side is not blameworthy. A measured retreat need not violate proper military practice.

XIANG-U-07-06.label: 07 師 小象 5
XIANG-U-07-06.original: 長子帥師，以中行也。弟子輿尸，使不當也。
XIANG-U-07-06.essay: The mature leader commands by the central way; placing an unfit younger man in charge invites casualties. Choosing the wrong commander has grave consequences.

XIANG-U-07-07.label: 07 師 小象 6
XIANG-U-07-07.original: 大君有命，以正功也。小人勿用，必亂邦也。
XIANG-U-07-07.essay: The great ruler apportions honors to recognize genuine achievement. Unworthy people must not be entrusted with government, lest they disrupt the state.

XIANG-U-08-01.label: 08 比 大象
XIANG-U-08-01.original: 地上有水，比；先王以建萬國，親諸侯。
XIANG-U-08-01.essay: Water spreads over Earth and joins with it. Former kings learned from this image to establish states and maintain close relationships with their regional lords.

XIANG-U-08-02.label: 08 比 小象 1
XIANG-U-08-02.essay: The first line’s sincere attachment may bring unexpected good fortune. Trust formed at the outset can attract help from beyond the original circle.

XIANG-U-08-03.label: 08 比 小象 2
XIANG-U-08-03.essay: Joining with others from a genuine inner commitment prevents self-betrayal. The relationship is sound because it begins in sincerity.

XIANG-U-08-04.label: 08 比 小象 3
XIANG-U-08-04.essay: Associating with the wrong people is a painful mistake. Companionship without judgment can injure rather than support a person.

XIANG-U-08-05.label: 08 比 小象 4
XIANG-U-08-05.essay: Openly aligning with the worthy outside oneself means following what is higher and better. Loyalty should attach to virtue, not mere familiarity.

XIANG-U-08-06.label: 08 比 小象 5
XIANG-U-08-06.original: 顯比之吉，位正中也。舍逆取順，失前禽也。邑人不誡，上使中也。
XIANG-U-08-06.essay: Visible alliance is fortunate because the ruler’s position is centered and correct. In the hunting image, what resists is released while what comes willingly is accepted; subjects feel no need for alarm.

XIANG-U-08-07.label: 08 比 小象 6
XIANG-U-08-07.essay: Association without a beginning or head cannot reach a proper conclusion. A community lacking a coherent basis has little prospect of lasting.

XIANG-U-09-01.label: 09 小畜 大象
XIANG-U-09-01.original: 風行天上，小畜，君子以懿文德。
XIANG-U-09-01.essay: Wind passes high across the sky, indicating a small gathering of strength. The exemplary person cultivates grace in conduct and refinement in character.

XIANG-U-09-02.label: 09 小畜 小象 1
XIANG-U-09-02.essay: Returning to one’s own right path is fortunate. The movement succeeds because it accords with what ought to be done.

XIANG-U-09-03.label: 09 小畜 小象 2
XIANG-U-09-03.essay: Being drawn back toward the right course still preserves the center. Joining others in correction need not mean losing independent judgment.

XIANG-U-09-04.label: 09 小畜 小象 3
XIANG-U-09-04.essay: The husband and wife turn against each other because the household relationship is not properly ordered. A damaged vehicle mirrors this internal discord.

XIANG-U-09-05.label: 09 小畜 小象 4
XIANG-U-09-05.essay: Sincerity helps fear and danger recede because the yielding line shares the purpose of those above. Trust gives cooperation practical force.

XIANG-U-09-06.label: 09 小畜 小象 5
XIANG-U-09-06.essay: Being bound together in good faith means not enjoying wealth alone. Prosperity has greater value when neighbors can share in it.

XIANG-U-09-07.label: 09 小畜 小象 6
XIANG-U-09-07.original: 既雨既處，德積載也。君子征凶，有所疑也。
XIANG-U-09-07.essay: Rain has finally fallen because virtue and resources have accumulated. Yet further advance is suspect: completion calls for caution, not a new reckless campaign.

XIANG-U-10-01.label: 10 履 大象
XIANG-U-10-01.original: 上天下澤，履；君子以辨上下，定民志。
XIANG-U-10-01.essay: Heaven stands above and the lake below, each in its proper place. The exemplary person clarifies roles and distinctions so that people understand their responsibilities.

XIANG-U-10-02.label: 10 履 小象 1
XIANG-U-10-02.essay: Walking simply on one’s own path fulfills a personal resolve. A modest start needs no borrowed grandeur.

XIANG-U-10-03.label: 10 履 小象 2
XIANG-U-10-03.essay: The secluded person stays fortunate because inner balance is not upset by outside demands. A tranquil path arises from steadiness of mind.

XIANG-U-10-04.label: 10 履 小象 3
XIANG-U-10-04.original: 眇能視，不足以有明也。跛能履，不足以與行也。咥人之凶，位不當也。武人為于大君，志剛也。
XIANG-U-10-04.essay: Weak vision cannot supply clarity, and impaired walking cannot keep pace. The tiger’s bite follows an unsuitable position; the warrior’s ambition is strong but unwise.

XIANG-U-10-05.label: 10 履 小象 4
XIANG-U-10-05.essay: Fearful caution while treading near the tiger brings a good ending. Such restraint enables the person’s intention to be fulfilled.

XIANG-U-10-06.label: 10 履 小象 5
XIANG-U-10-06.essay: Decisive walking remains dangerous even in a proper position. Rank and authority do not cancel the need to consider the consequences of firmness.

XIANG-U-10-07.label: 10 履 小象 6
XIANG-U-10-07.essay: Great fortune at the top signifies a cause for widespread celebration. Looking back over one’s conduct allows a fitting completion.

XIANG-U-11-01.label: 11 泰 大象
XIANG-U-11-01.original: 天地交，泰；后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。
XIANG-U-11-01.essay: Heaven and Earth exchange their influences, producing peace and growth. The ruler supports this process by helping nature’s work and ensuring that people benefit from it.

XIANG-U-11-02.label: 11 泰 小象 1
XIANG-U-11-02.essay: Pulling up grass brings its roots and companion shoots. Going forward together is fortunate because the group’s intention reaches beyond itself.

XIANG-U-11-03.label: 11 泰 小象 2
XIANG-U-11-03.original: 包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也。
XIANG-U-11-03.essay: Broad-minded conduct accords with the middle way and makes virtue shine more widely. Inclusion must be joined to fairness.

XIANG-U-11-04.label: 11 泰 小象 3
XIANG-U-11-04.essay: Nothing moves outward without eventually returning. Rise and decline belong to the changing boundary between Heaven and Earth.

XIANG-U-11-05.label: 11 泰 小象 4
XIANG-U-11-05.original: 翩翩不富，皆失實也。不戒以孚，中心願也。
XIANG-U-11-05.essay: Neighbors descend lightly without relying on wealth. Their trust reflects a heartfelt desire for fellowship rather than a calculated bargain.

XIANG-U-11-06.label: 11 泰 小象 5
XIANG-U-11-06.essay: The marriage alliance brings exceptional fortune because a centered intention can be carried out. Proper relationships translate purpose into action.

XIANG-U-11-07.label: 11 泰 小象 6
XIANG-U-11-07.essay: When a wall collapses back into the moat, government commands have become confused. The image warns that established order can break apart.

XIANG-U-12-01.label: 12 否 大象
XIANG-U-12-01.original: 天地不交，否；君子以儉德辟難，不可榮以祿。
XIANG-U-12-01.essay: Heaven and Earth fail to communicate, illustrating stagnation. The exemplary person reduces outward display, preserves integrity, and refuses honors that would expose him to danger.

XIANG-U-12-02.label: 12 否 小象 1
XIANG-U-12-02.essay: The grass and its roots hold together in upright resolve. Even during obstruction, the intention remains directed toward a worthy ruler.

XIANG-U-12-03.label: 12 否 小象 2
XIANG-U-12-03.essay: A great person bears stagnation without mingling indiscriminately with the crowd. Keeping principle intact matters more than fitting in.

XIANG-U-12-04.label: 12 否 小象 3
XIANG-U-12-04.essay: Concealed shame results from occupying an unsuitable position. A compromised role can force a person to hide what ought to be corrected.

XIANG-U-12-05.label: 12 否 小象 4
XIANG-U-12-05.essay: Acting under a legitimate mandate is free from blame and allows the underlying purpose to advance.

XIANG-U-12-06.label: 12 否 小象 5
XIANG-U-12-06.essay: The great person’s favorable outcome comes from occupying the correct position. Authority must remain aligned with responsibility.

XIANG-U-12-07.label: 12 否 小象 6
XIANG-U-12-07.essay: Stagnation eventually overturns; it cannot last forever. A blocked situation contains the possibility of its own reversal.

XIANG-U-13-01.label: 13 同人 大象
XIANG-U-13-01.original: 天與火，同人；君子以類族辨物。
XIANG-U-13-01.essay: Heaven and fire rise together in the image of fellowship. The exemplary person groups people and things by kind while recognizing the distinctions between them.

XIANG-U-13-02.label: 13 同人 小象 1
XIANG-U-13-02.essay: Going beyond the gate to join with others gives no cause for reproach. Genuine fellowship should not be limited to one household.

XIANG-U-13-03.label: 13 同人 小象 2
XIANG-U-13-03.essay: Associating only with one’s own clan is regrettable. Such narrow loyalty restricts the possibility of wider cooperation.

XIANG-U-13-04.label: 13 同人 小象 3
XIANG-U-13-04.original: 伏戎于莽，敵剛也。三歲不興，安行也。
XIANG-U-13-04.essay: Troops hidden in brushwood confront a strong opponent. Their failure to move for three years reveals the danger and difficulty of that opposition.

XIANG-U-13-05.label: 13 同人 小象 4
XIANG-U-13-05.original: 乘其墉，義弗克也，其吉，則困而反則也。
XIANG-U-13-05.essay: Climbing the wall but refraining from attack means accepting that assault is not justified. Restraint allows the person to return to the appropriate rule.

XIANG-U-13-06.label: 13 同人 小象 5
XIANG-U-13-06.original: 同人之先，以中直也。大師相遇，言相克也。
XIANG-U-13-06.essay: The early tears of the allied people reflect honest inner purpose. After overcoming opposition, the armies can finally meet.

XIANG-U-13-07.label: 13 同人 小象 6
XIANG-U-13-07.essay: Fellowship on the outskirts carries no regret, but the larger aspiration remains unrealized. Peaceful contact is not yet complete unity.

XIANG-U-14-01.label: 14 大有 大象
XIANG-U-14-01.original: 火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。
XIANG-U-14-01.essay: Fire shines high in Heaven, indicating great possession. The exemplary person restrains harmful conduct, promotes goodness, and honors Heaven’s favorable charge.

XIANG-U-14-02.label: 14 大有 小象 1
XIANG-U-14-02.essay: At the beginning of great possession, harmful association has not yet formed. Keeping clear of corrupt influence preserves one’s advantage.

XIANG-U-14-03.label: 14 大有 小象 2
XIANG-U-14-03.essay: A large wagon can carry heavy stores because its load is held securely at the center. Resources require dependable support.

XIANG-U-14-04.label: 14 大有 小象 3
XIANG-U-14-04.original: 公用亨于天子，小人害也。
XIANG-U-14-04.essay: A duke’s offering to the Son of Heaven entails responsibilities a petty person cannot bear. High honors without suitable character bring harm.

XIANG-U-14-05.label: 14 大有 小象 4
XIANG-U-14-05.essay: Refraining from ostentation avoids blame because the person sees the situation clearly. Knowing what not to display is a form of discernment.

XIANG-U-14-06.label: 14 大有 小象 5
XIANG-U-14-06.original: 厥孚交如，信以發志也。威如之吉，易而无備也。
XIANG-U-14-06.essay: Authentic trust inspires purpose, while appropriate dignity prevents complacency. Authority can remain accessible without surrendering necessary care.

XIANG-U-14-07.label: 14 大有 小象 6
XIANG-U-14-07.essay: Great good fortune at the summit is described as help from Heaven. The blessing is associated with worthy conduct rather than mere accumulation.

XIANG-U-15-01.label: 15 謙 大象
XIANG-U-15-01.original: 地中有山，謙；君子以裒多益寡，稱物平施。
XIANG-U-15-01.essay: A mountain rests within Earth, a picture of modesty. The exemplary person reduces what is excessive and adds to what is lacking, distributing things fairly.

XIANG-U-15-02.label: 15 謙 小象 1
XIANG-U-15-02.essay: The deeply modest person governs the self through humility. Self-respect does not require superiority over others.

XIANG-U-15-03.label: 15 謙 小象 2
XIANG-U-15-03.essay: Expressed modesty is fortunate because it comes from the heart. Genuine humility is an inward attainment, not a performance.

XIANG-U-15-04.label: 15 謙 小象 3
XIANG-U-15-04.essay: A worker who remains modest despite achievement gains the trust of the people. Earned authority has no need of boasting.

XIANG-U-15-05.label: 15 謙 小象 4
XIANG-U-15-05.essay: Actively showing modesty is favorable because it does not violate proper rules. Courtesy and effectiveness can coexist.

XIANG-U-15-06.label: 15 謙 小象 5
XIANG-U-15-06.essay: The expedition is directed against those who refuse proper order. In its ancient political setting, humility does not mean surrendering responsibility.

XIANG-U-15-07.label: 15 謙 小象 6
XIANG-U-15-07.original: 鳴謙，志未得也。可用行師，征邑國也。
XIANG-U-15-07.essay: Although modest conduct is well known, the aspiration is still not wholly achieved. The permitted military action concerns restoring order in one’s own territory.

XIANG-U-16-01.label: 16 豫 大象
XIANG-U-16-01.original: 雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。
XIANG-U-16-01.essay: Thunder breaks forth from Earth, creating an image of joyful movement. Ancient kings established music to honor virtue and offered solemn sacrifices to Heaven and the ancestors.

XIANG-U-16-02.label: 16 豫 小象 1
XIANG-U-16-02.essay: Voicing delight too proudly leads to misfortune when ambition has reached its limit. Satisfaction should not become self-glorification.

XIANG-U-16-03.label: 16 豫 小象 2
XIANG-U-16-03.essay: Not waiting even a whole day to distinguish what is right is fortunate. Clear judgment comes from an inwardly centered and upright position.

XIANG-U-16-04.label: 16 豫 小象 3
XIANG-U-16-04.essay: Looking upward in restless pursuit of pleasure produces regret because the position is unsuitable. Approval-seeking disturbs good judgment.

XIANG-U-16-05.label: 16 豫 小象 4
XIANG-U-16-05.essay: The great gathering around a source of enthusiasm allows a far-reaching purpose to be realized. Trust turns common joy into collective achievement.

XIANG-U-16-06.label: 16 豫 小象 5
XIANG-U-16-06.original: 六五貞疾，乘剛也。恆不死，中未亡也。
XIANG-U-16-06.essay: Persistent illness in the fifth line comes from resting above a firm line. The central position nevertheless prevents total collapse.

XIANG-U-16-07.label: 16 豫 小象 6
XIANG-U-16-07.essay: Blind delight at the top cannot endure. Enjoyment disconnected from judgment eventually becomes exhausted.

XIANG-U-17-01.label: 17 隨 大象
XIANG-U-17-01.original: 澤中有雷，隨；君子以嚮晦入宴息。
XIANG-U-17-01.essay: Thunder rests within the lake. The exemplary person follows the rhythm of the day, withdrawing at dusk to rest rather than forcing continuous activity.

XIANG-U-17-02.label: 17 隨 小象 1
XIANG-U-17-02.original: 官有渝，從正吉也。出門交有功，不失也。
XIANG-U-17-02.essay: A change of office is favorable if it follows what is right. Going outside to form relationships can produce results without compromising one’s principles.

XIANG-U-17-03.label: 17 隨 小象 2
XIANG-U-17-03.essay: Binding oneself to the child excludes the grown man. Not every competing attachment can be maintained at the same time.

XIANG-U-17-04.label: 17 隨 小象 3
XIANG-U-17-04.essay: Following the mature person means leaving the lesser attachment behind. The direction of one’s loyalty shapes what is possible.

XIANG-U-17-05.label: 17 隨 小象 4
XIANG-U-17-05.original: 隨有獲，其義凶也。有孚在道，明功也。
XIANG-U-17-05.essay: Gaining followers can be dangerous when acquisition becomes an end in itself. Sincere adherence to the way makes the purpose clear.

XIANG-U-17-06.label: 17 隨 小象 5
XIANG-U-17-06.essay: Trust placed in what is excellent is fortunate because the position is right and central. The quality of what one follows matters.

XIANG-U-17-07.label: 17 隨 小象 6
XIANG-U-17-07.essay: Binding and tying someone at the very top shows that the situation has gone too far. Forced attachment cannot continue without limit.

XIANG-U-18-01.label: 18 蠱 大象
XIANG-U-18-01.original: 山下有風，蠱；君子以振民育德。
XIANG-U-18-01.essay: Wind moves beneath a mountain, stirring up what has decayed. The exemplary person awakens the community and cultivates character in order to correct entrenched faults.

XIANG-U-18-02.label: 18 蠱 小象 1
XIANG-U-18-02.essay: Repairing the father’s mistakes is ultimately an act of honoring the parent. Responsible succession includes correcting inherited damage.

XIANG-U-18-03.label: 18 蠱 小象 2
XIANG-U-18-03.essay: Remedying the mother’s errors calls for a balanced approach. Harsh insistence would violate the proper middle way.

XIANG-U-18-04.label: 18 蠱 小象 3
XIANG-U-18-04.essay: Working to repair the father’s mistakes may bring small regrets, but the conclusion need not involve serious blame.

XIANG-U-18-05.label: 18 蠱 小象 4
XIANG-U-18-05.essay: Indulging the father’s faults fails to accomplish the needed change. Continued delay carries regret.

XIANG-U-18-06.label: 18 蠱 小象 5
XIANG-U-18-06.essay: Correcting inherited mistakes with integrity earns respect. Honor arises when the successor carries forward what is worthy.

XIANG-U-18-07.label: 18 蠱 小象 6
XIANG-U-18-07.essay: Not serving kings and nobles can express an example-worthy resolve. Independence may preserve a moral purpose beyond office.

XIANG-U-19-01.label: 19 臨 大象
XIANG-U-19-01.original: 澤上有地，臨；君子以教思无窮，容保民无疆。
XIANG-U-19-01.essay: Earth lies above the lake, portraying attentive approach. The exemplary person teaches tirelessly and protects the people with enduring generosity.

XIANG-U-19-02.label: 19 臨 小象 1
XIANG-U-19-02.essay: Approaching others through sympathetic understanding is fortunate because the purpose advances in a right direction.

XIANG-U-19-03.label: 19 臨 小象 2
XIANG-U-19-03.original: 咸臨，吉无不利；未順命也。
XIANG-U-19-03.essay: The second sympathetic approach is favorable, yet does not simply submit to command. Genuine responsiveness retains independent judgment.

XIANG-U-19-04.label: 19 臨 小象 3
XIANG-U-19-04.original: 甘臨，位不當也。既憂之，咎不長也。
XIANG-U-19-04.essay: Sweet words without substance arise from an unsuitable position. Recognizing this failing and becoming concerned can keep the error from lasting.

XIANG-U-19-05.label: 19 臨 小象 4
XIANG-U-19-05.essay: Arriving with full attention brings no blame because the position fits the task. Presence must be matched by appropriate conduct.

XIANG-U-19-06.label: 19 臨 小象 5
XIANG-U-19-06.essay: A wise ruler acts through the middle way. Sound oversight is neither neglectful nor excessively controlling.

XIANG-U-19-07.label: 19 臨 小象 6
XIANG-U-19-07.essay: Generous and substantial approach is fortunate because the intention comes from within. Care for others must be deeply rooted.

XIANG-U-20-01.label: 20 觀 大象
XIANG-U-20-01.original: 風行地上，觀；先王以省方，觀民設教。
XIANG-U-20-01.essay: Wind travels across Earth, making conditions visible. Early kings inspected different regions and then adapted their instruction to the people they observed.

XIANG-U-20-02.label: 20 觀 小象 1
XIANG-U-20-02.essay: A childlike way of looking sees little beyond appearances. For an ordinary person that may be understandable, but a responsible leader should know better.

XIANG-U-20-03.label: 20 觀 小象 2
XIANG-U-20-03.essay: Looking through a narrow opening is a limited viewpoint. The commentary criticizes such restricted observation in the language of its own age.

XIANG-U-20-04.label: 20 觀 小象 3
XIANG-U-20-04.essay: Examining one’s own life helps determine whether to advance or withdraw. Thoughtful self-observation keeps a person from losing the way.

XIANG-U-20-05.label: 20 觀 小象 4
XIANG-U-20-05.essay: Observing the splendor of a state suggests honorable service as the ruler’s guest. Recognition must reflect genuine merit.

XIANG-U-20-06.label: 20 觀 小象 5
XIANG-U-20-06.essay: A ruler who examines personal conduct should also observe the condition of the people. The public response reveals the effects of government.

XIANG-U-20-07.label: 20 觀 小象 6
XIANG-U-20-07.essay: Looking at the lives of others still requires an unsettled conscience. Even from a higher position, vigilance and reflection remain necessary.

XIANG-U-21-01.label: 21 噬嗑 大象
XIANG-U-21-01.original: 雷電噬嗑；先王以明罰敕法。
XIANG-U-21-01.essay: Thunder and lightning accompany each other, the image of biting through obstruction. Ancient rulers made penalties clear and established enforceable laws.

XIANG-U-21-02.label: 21 噬嗑 小象 1
XIANG-U-21-02.essay: Stocks that cover the toes keep a wrongdoer from continuing. Early correction can stop a harmful course before it grows.

XIANG-U-21-03.label: 21 噬嗑 小象 2
XIANG-U-21-03.essay: Biting through soft flesh until the nose sinks in indicates force applied close at hand. The yielding line acts above a firm one.

XIANG-U-21-04.label: 21 噬嗑 小象 3
XIANG-U-21-04.essay: Encountering poison results from being in the wrong place. The difficulty of enforcing order can arise from the enforcer’s own position.

XIANG-U-21-05.label: 21 噬嗑 小象 4
XIANG-U-21-05.essay: Perseverance through difficulty is fortunate, although the work has not yet reached full clarity. Punishment alone is not complete justice.

XIANG-U-21-06.label: 21 噬嗑 小象 5
XIANG-U-21-06.essay: Careful constancy amid danger avoids blame because the action fits its circumstances. The right measure is crucial.

XIANG-U-21-07.label: 21 噬嗑 小象 6
XIANG-U-21-07.essay: A heavy collar covering the ears shows a failure to listen and understand. Severe punishment follows persistent moral deafness.

XIANG-U-22-01.label: 22 賁 大象
XIANG-U-22-01.original: 山下有火，賁；君子以明庶政，无敢折獄。
XIANG-U-22-01.essay: Fire brightens the mountain’s foot, suggesting ornament and illumination. The exemplary person clarifies routine public affairs but does not hastily decide major criminal cases.

XIANG-U-22-02.label: 22 賁 小象 1
XIANG-U-22-02.essay: Leaving the carriage and walking is a deliberate rejection of an improper privilege. A choice can be dignified precisely because it is modest.

XIANG-U-22-03.label: 22 賁 小象 2
XIANG-U-22-03.essay: Adorning the beard depends on what stands above it. Ornament is secondary to the person or substance that it embellishes.

XIANG-U-22-04.label: 22 賁 小象 3
XIANG-U-22-04.essay: Long-lasting correctness brings good fortune because no one can ultimately diminish it. True beauty rests on integrity.

XIANG-U-22-05.label: 22 賁 小象 4
XIANG-U-22-05.original: 六四，當位疑也。匪寇婚媾，終无尤也。
XIANG-U-22-05.essay: The fourth line’s uncertainty comes from its position. What seemed threatening turns out to be a marriage proposal, and the matter ends without reproach.

XIANG-U-22-06.label: 22 賁 小象 5
XIANG-U-22-06.essay: The fifth line’s good fortune brings joy. Simple gifts offered sincerely can be more fitting than lavish display.

XIANG-U-22-07.label: 22 賁 小象 6
XIANG-U-22-07.essay: Plain white ornament avoids blame because aspiration at the top has found its proper expression. Simplicity completes refinement.

XIANG-U-23-01.label: 23 剝 大象
XIANG-U-23-01.original: 山附地上，剝；上以厚下，安宅。
XIANG-U-23-01.essay: A mountain rises upon Earth, yet its base must remain secure. Those in authority should strengthen and support the people below so that homes remain safe.

XIANG-U-23-02.label: 23 剝 小象 1
XIANG-U-23-02.essay: The bed begins to be stripped at its feet. Weakening the foundation destroys what supports everything above.

XIANG-U-23-03.label: 23 剝 小象 2
XIANG-U-23-03.essay: As the bed is stripped further, no effective allies remain. Deterioration spreads when no one can provide support.

XIANG-U-23-04.label: 23 剝 小象 3
XIANG-U-23-04.essay: One can separate from the forces of disintegration without blame. This departure cuts ties with what is failing above and below.

XIANG-U-23-05.label: 23 剝 小象 4
XIANG-U-23-05.essay: The damage has reached the skin, making disaster immediate. What began beneath the surface can no longer be ignored.

XIANG-U-23-06.label: 23 剝 小象 5
XIANG-U-23-06.essay: Orderly favor shown to the palace women brings no final reproach. Proper arrangement can limit conflict during an unstable time.

XIANG-U-23-07.label: 23 剝 小象 6
XIANG-U-23-07.original: 君子得輿，民所載也。小人剝廬，終不可用也。
XIANG-U-23-07.essay: The exemplary person receives a carriage because the people support him; the petty person loses even his shelter. The contrast concerns the consequences of conduct.

XIANG-U-24-01.label: 24 復 大象
XIANG-U-24-01.original: 雷在地中，復；先王以至日閉關，商旅不行，后不省方。
XIANG-U-24-01.essay: Thunder lies hidden in Earth, indicating the beginning of a return. At the turning of the season, ancient kings closed the passes and allowed people and rulers to rest.

XIANG-U-24-02.label: 24 復 小象 1
XIANG-U-24-02.essay: Returning before one has strayed far permits moral self-cultivation. Small errors are easier to repair when recognized early.

XIANG-U-24-03.label: 24 復 小象 2
XIANG-U-24-03.essay: The auspicious return is accompanied by a humble concern for others. Renewed goodness is strengthened through benevolence.

XIANG-U-24-04.label: 24 復 小象 3
XIANG-U-24-04.essay: Repeatedly turning back can be perilous, but the intention to correct oneself is not blameworthy. Recovery may require several attempts.

XIANG-U-24-05.label: 24 復 小象 4
XIANG-U-24-05.essay: Walking among others, one person returns alone because of commitment to the right path. Conscience may require independent action.

XIANG-U-24-06.label: 24 復 小象 5
XIANG-U-24-06.essay: A substantial return leaves no regret because the person examines the self from a centered standpoint.

XIANG-U-24-07.label: 24 復 小象 6
XIANG-U-24-07.essay: Being lost and unable to return is disastrous because it opposes the way a ruler should follow. Persistent error eventually affects the whole community.

XIANG-U-25-01.label: 25 无妄 大象
XIANG-U-25-01.original: 天下雷行，物與无妄；先王以茂對時，育萬物。
XIANG-U-25-01.essay: Thunder moves beneath Heaven, and all things proceed without falsity. Ancient rulers responded attentively to the season and nourished living beings.

XIANG-U-25-02.label: 25 无妄 小象 1
XIANG-U-25-02.essay: Going forward without delusion allows an honest purpose to be fulfilled. Right action begins without contrivance.

XIANG-U-25-03.label: 25 无妄 小象 2
XIANG-U-25-03.essay: Not farming solely for the harvest shows freedom from a calculating expectation of wealth. Work should follow what is appropriate, not only immediate gain.

XIANG-U-25-04.label: 25 无妄 小象 3
XIANG-U-25-04.essay: The passerby gets the cow, but the townspeople suffer the loss. Misfortune may fall on those who did not cause the event.

XIANG-U-25-05.label: 25 无妄 小象 4
XIANG-U-25-05.essay: Firmly preserving what is right brings no blame. Constancy matters especially when the circumstances are uncertain.

XIANG-U-25-06.label: 25 无妄 小象 5
XIANG-U-25-06.essay: The illness that occurs without wrongdoing should not prompt indiscriminate remedies. In this textual setting the warning is against needless intervention, not modern medical care.

XIANG-U-25-07.label: 25 无妄 小象 6
XIANG-U-25-07.essay: Acting without delusion can still bring misfortune when the course has reached its limit. Good intentions cannot erase the demands of timing.

XIANG-U-26-01.label: 26 大畜 大象
XIANG-U-26-01.original: 天在山中，大畜；君子以多識前言往行，以畜其德。
XIANG-U-26-01.essay: Heaven appears enclosed within a mountain, the image of great accumulation. The exemplary person studies the words and deeds of earlier generations to deepen personal character.

XIANG-U-26-02.label: 26 大畜 小象 1
XIANG-U-26-02.essay: When danger lies ahead, stopping is beneficial. Restraint keeps one from entering an avoidable disaster.

XIANG-U-26-03.label: 26 大畜 小象 2
XIANG-U-26-03.essay: The carriage loses its axle fitting, yet inner balance keeps this from becoming a moral fault. Temporary immobility may be necessary.

XIANG-U-26-04.label: 26 大畜 小象 3
XIANG-U-26-04.essay: Going forward becomes advantageous when the intention agrees with those above. Preparation and disciplined strength make advancement fitting.

XIANG-U-26-05.label: 26 大畜 小象 4
XIANG-U-26-05.essay: The fourth line brings great fortune and joy. Restraining harmful power while it is young prevents later injury.

XIANG-U-26-06.label: 26 大畜 小象 5
XIANG-U-26-06.essay: The fifth line’s good fortune is a cause for celebration. Managing the source of danger is wiser than fighting its symptoms.

XIANG-U-26-07.label: 26 大畜 小象 6
XIANG-U-26-07.essay: The open road across Heaven indicates that the way can now be widely carried out. What was restrained has found constructive release.

XIANG-U-27-01.label: 27 頤 大象
XIANG-U-27-01.original: 山下有雷，頤；君子以慎言語，節飲食。
XIANG-U-27-01.essay: Thunder stirs beneath the mountain, creating the image of nourishment. The exemplary person watches speech carefully and practices moderation in food and drink.

XIANG-U-27-02.label: 27 頤 小象 1
XIANG-U-27-02.essay: Staring at another person’s food after abandoning one’s own resources is hardly admirable. Desire can undermine self-sufficiency.

XIANG-U-27-03.label: 27 頤 小象 2
XIANG-U-27-03.essay: The second line’s journey is unfortunate because it departs from its proper company. Seeking support in the wrong place creates dependence.

XIANG-U-27-04.label: 27 頤 小象 3
XIANG-U-27-04.essay: Being unable to nourish oneself properly for ten years shows a profound departure from the right way. The problem is structural, not momentary.

XIANG-U-27-05.label: 27 頤 小象 4
XIANG-U-27-05.essay: The fourth line’s reversed search for nourishment is fortunate because help from above can be shared openly. The higher position extends its benefits.

XIANG-U-27-06.label: 27 頤 小象 5
XIANG-U-27-06.essay: The fifth line is fortunate in staying steady and following a suitable guide. Dependence can be appropriate when exercised with humility.

XIANG-U-27-07.label: 27 頤 小象 6
XIANG-U-27-07.essay: Nourishment originating from the top may be dangerous but fortunate, and it brings broad blessing. Great responsibility accompanies the ability to sustain others.

XIANG-U-28-01.label: 28 大過 大象
XIANG-U-28-01.original: 澤滅木，大過。君子以獨立不懼，遯世无悶。
XIANG-U-28-01.essay: The lake rises above the trees and overwhelms them. The exemplary person stands independently without fear, and can withdraw from public life without resentment.

XIANG-U-28-02.label: 28 大過 小象 1
XIANG-U-28-02.essay: Using white reeds as a mat expresses care and gentleness at the foundation. Deliberate preparation reduces the chance of harm.

XIANG-U-28-03.label: 28 大過 小象 2
XIANG-U-28-03.essay: An old man marrying a young woman is presented as an unusual pairing. The commentary highlights a relationship that crosses an ordinary boundary.

XIANG-U-28-04.label: 28 大過 小象 3
XIANG-U-28-04.original: 棟橈之凶，不可以有輔也。
XIANG-U-28-04.essay: A sagging roof beam spells danger because nothing adequately supports it. A structure cannot survive indefinitely without reinforcement.

XIANG-U-28-05.label: 28 大過 小象 4
XIANG-U-28-05.essay: The raised, firm beam is fortunate because it no longer bends beneath the load. Sound support makes strength useful.

XIANG-U-28-06.label: 28 大過 小象 5
XIANG-U-28-06.original: 枯楊生華，何可久也。老婦士夫，亦可丑也。
XIANG-U-28-06.essay: Flowers on an old poplar cannot last; likewise the pairing of an older woman and younger man is treated as irregular in the ancient text. Brief flourishing is not the same as enduring renewal.

XIANG-U-28-07.label: 28 大過 小象 6
XIANG-U-28-07.essay: Crossing water so deeply that it covers the head is dangerous, yet the deed is not necessarily blameworthy. The commentary distinguishes harmful outcomes from culpable intentions.

XIANG-U-29-01.label: 29 坎 大象
XIANG-U-29-01.original: 水洊至，習坎；君子以常德行，習教事。
XIANG-U-29-01.essay: Water follows water in successive depths, an image of repeated danger. The exemplary person keeps conduct steady and rehearses teaching and public duties.

XIANG-U-29-02.label: 29 坎 小象 1
XIANG-U-29-02.essay: Falling deeper into the pit is disastrous because the right path has been lost. Repeated exposure to danger does not make an error harmless.

XIANG-U-29-03.label: 29 坎 小象 2
XIANG-U-29-03.essay: Only a small gain is possible because the person has not yet escaped the middle of the danger. Ambition must be scaled to reality.

XIANG-U-29-04.label: 29 坎 小象 3
XIANG-U-29-04.essay: Moving from one pit to another accomplishes nothing in the end. Action without a safe route only multiplies exposure.

XIANG-U-29-05.label: 29 坎 小象 4
XIANG-U-29-05.essay: The simple offering of wine and food works through cooperation between firmness and gentleness. Sincerity can matter more than display.

XIANG-U-29-06.label: 29 坎 小象 5
XIANG-U-29-06.essay: The pit is not yet full because the central position has not reached its full measure. Relief is partial and restraint remains necessary.

XIANG-U-29-07.label: 29 坎 小象 6
XIANG-U-29-07.essay: The final line spends three years in danger because the proper way has been lost. Prolonged confinement is the result of failing to correct course.

XIANG-U-30-01.label: 30 離 大象
XIANG-U-30-01.original: 明兩作離，大人以繼明照于四方。
XIANG-U-30-01.essay: Light shines twice, the image of repeated fire. A great person carries illumination onward so that its beneficial influence reaches the four directions.

XIANG-U-30-02.label: 30 離 小象 1
XIANG-U-30-02.essay: Carefulness amid confused steps prevents blame. Respectful attention is essential when clarity is not yet established.

XIANG-U-30-03.label: 30 離 小象 2
XIANG-U-30-03.essay: Yellow light brings great good fortune because it occupies the central path. Balanced brightness is more reliable than dazzling display.

XIANG-U-30-04.label: 30 離 小象 3
XIANG-U-30-04.essay: The setting sun cannot remain at its height. The commentary points to the inevitable limits of a passing stage.

XIANG-U-30-05.label: 30 離 小象 4
XIANG-U-30-05.essay: A sudden flare cannot find a lasting place. A force that appears violently may disappear just as quickly.

XIANG-U-30-06.label: 30 離 小象 5
XIANG-U-30-06.essay: The fifth line’s good fortune is linked to the ruler’s position. Grief and vigilance can accompany responsible authority.

XIANG-U-30-07.label: 30 離 小象 6
XIANG-U-30-07.essay: The ruler’s expedition seeks to rectify the state. The proper purpose of coercive force, in this classical account, is to restore just order.

XIANG-L-31-01.label: 31 咸 大象
XIANG-L-31-01.original: 山上有澤，咸；君子以虛受人。
XIANG-L-31-01.essay: A lake rests upon a mountain: this is Influence. The exemplary person welcomes others with an open and receptive mind.

XIANG-L-31-02.label: 31 咸 小象 1
XIANG-L-31-02.essay: The stirring of the big toe shows that the intention is already directed outward, although movement has barely begun.

XIANG-L-31-03.label: 31 咸 小象 2
XIANG-L-31-03.essay: Remaining still is fortunate even amid danger, because yielding appropriately avoids harm.

XIANG-L-31-04.label: 31 咸 小象 3
XIANG-L-31-04.original: 咸其股，亦不處也。志在隨人，所執下也。
XIANG-L-31-04.essay: Feeling the influence in the thighs prevents remaining still; merely following others reveals a low and dependent purpose.

XIANG-L-31-05.label: 31 咸 小象 4
XIANG-L-31-05.original: 貞吉悔亡，未感害也。憧憧往來，未光大也。
